## Verdict: adopt with conditions

Run it as a time-boxed pilot on a few machines, pinned to the Claude Code version it was tested on. Don't roll it out to the whole team yet.

I read the README, the hook contract (`docs/hooks.md`), the hook wiring, the plugin launcher script, the changelog and the delivery benchmark's results and limits. I did not run the test suite or install it.

## Reasons

- **It addresses a real gap in your setup.** You mix four models and use subagents heavily, and that is exactly where the built-in options fall short. In the tool's own benchmark (Claude Code 2.1.330), a user `CLAUDE.md` reached only 46.9% (60 of 128) of subagent requests, and `.claude/rules` also reached 46.9%. Both also give every model the other models' rules (`README.md:42-47`). `CLAUDE.md` never reaches the built-in Explore and Plan subagents.
- **Its delivery record is strong, but only for one version and a simulated API.** It delivered the right rules to 3,090 of 3,090 requests that had rules due, 763 of 763 of them from subagents, across 299 generated sessions. Those were real Claude Code sessions, but the API was a local stand-in, so no model ever answered (`README.md:29-32`). The result was checked against noonsight's own rule-matching logic, so a wrong match would not show up there (`experiments/delivery/README.md:272`).
- **The rules themselves have weak evidence.** A rule with a measured effect gets the model to do something specific, for example `verify-changes` made Sonnet/Haiku run the tests after editing in 29 of 30 runs, against 0 of 30 without it. But no quality gain was shown: a paid pilot found 133/144 tasks passed with no rules, 132/144 under noonsight, and 133/144 with a `CLAUDE.md` holding every model's rules (`README.md:224`). None of the Opus 5.5 rules has a measured effect. Those tasks were small.
- **Out of the box it does little for Opus and Fable.** Their rules for attended sessions ship turned off, so your interactive sessions on those models get nothing from the preset until you turn rules on (`README.md:52`). The value you get depends on writing your own rules.
- **It doesn't get in the way.** The hooks never block a call, always exit successfully, and each has a 10-second timeout. It has no runtime dependencies. It changes an agent call only when the optional routing feature is on. `NOONSIGHT_DISABLE=1` turns it off for a session (`docs/hooks.md:10-25`).
- **It is young and depends on undocumented behavior.** It is at version 0.1.0, with a single upstream repo (`bpsanti/noonsight`). Handling of forks, unattended sessions and subagents relies on Claude Code internals that aren't documented (`forkedFrom`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED=0`, the `toolUseId` in subagent metadata, `state.json` in background jobs) (`docs/hooks.md:123,168,330`). The benchmark itself found nine of the tool's own bugs (F1 to F9) in the runs before the current one; all are now fixed.

## Conditions and risks

**What would have to hold:**
- You run Claude Code 2.1.330, or you re-run its delivery benchmark (`npm run test:live` plus `experiments/delivery`) on each Claude Code version you upgrade to. Its results only hold for the version they ran on (`README.md:26`).
- Someone owns the rule files and checks `noonsight report` to drop rules that never change anything visible.
- Everyone on the team installs it the same way: npm global, not `npx`, which stops delivering once the npm cache is cleared. Each person runs `noonsight trust` in each shared repo.
- You set `session.unattended_when_env` for interactive sessions nobody watches (for example, ones an orchestrator starts), and set `NOONSIGHT_SCOPE` where you want the scoped rules.
- You're on the Anthropic API, or you pin the `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL` variables. On Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry, model aliases point to other models and the hook only warns.
- Ideally, run your own A/B test of your actual rules on your own tasks before rolling out widely.

**What could go wrong:**
- **Silent gaps:**
  - Workflow agents get nothing.
  - Agent-team teammates in split panes were never tested.
  - Subagents from plugins your organization syncs are predicted on the wrong model; the tool only warns about the mismatch afterwards.
  - Sessions on `default` or `opusplan`, or with a model set only in an MDM profile, can't be resolved.
  - When several subagents of the same type start at once and need different rules, each gets nothing until its first Edit, Write or agent call.
- **Breaks when Claude Code changes:** a Claude Code update can quietly change hook behavior it depends on.
- **Cost:** `verify-changes` roughly doubled cost per run on the small fix task ($0.0505 vs $0.0240 for Sonnet). Opus and Fable rules that ship off are documented as adding about 20% to 80% more output tokens.
- **macOS:** it reads the `claude` command line through `ps`. A prompt containing `--model x` can't be told apart from the real option; that case produces a warning, not a wrong guess.
- **Footprint:** `noonsight install` changes the settings of every Claude Code login on the account. It also writes state under `~/.local/state/noonsight/`, including a decision log of up to 2×20 MB.
- **Other side effects:**
  - `/fork` stops working in sessions started with `noonsight run`.
  - With routing on in auto mode, the other agent calls in the same response get refused and have to be made again.
  - The optional classifier sends the first 4,000 characters of each task through your login.

## What it guarantees

noonsight guarantees only **delivery**: each session and subagent gets the rules declared for the model it actually runs on in its context, and gets them again after a model switch, compaction, clear, resume or fork. It does not guarantee the model follows them. That guarantee rests on undocumented Claude Code hook behavior, checked only on Claude Code 2.1.330 against a stand-in API, and it excludes the gaps listed above.

**Verdict: adopt with conditions.** Run it as a time-boxed pilot on a few machines, not a team-wide rollout.

- **It fits your setup.** It delivers rules per model to sessions and subagents, and re-delivers on `/model`, `/compact`, `/clear`, resume and fork. Its own guidance is to skip it when every session runs one model.
- **Subagents are where it beats `CLAUDE.md`.** In its benchmark a user `CLAUDE.md` reached 60 of 128 subagent requests and never reaches Explore or Plan subagents. noonsight reports 763 of 763.
- **It keeps other models' rules out.** A shared `CLAUDE.md` gave each model mostly other models' rules (about 33% of the rule text was its own). noonsight's figure was 79%, with the remainder retired by a note after a model switch.
- **No quality gain is shown.** The paid pilot resolved 133 of 144 tasks without rules, 132 with noonsight and 133 with a `CLAUDE.md`. That pilot delivered to the main conversation only, so it does not test the subagent case.
- **Measured rule effects are narrow.** On small tasks, `verify-changes` made Sonnet and Haiku run the tests after editing (29 of 30 against 0 of 30 on Sonnet). No Opus rule has a measured effect, and the only Fable effect is shorter sentences in reports.
- **Out of the box, your Opus and Fable interactive sessions get nothing.** Their attended rules ship off. Sonnet and Haiku get `verify-changes` only after a tracked code edit. The value for you is mostly in rules you write yourselves.
- **It is one week old.** It is version 0.1.0 from a single author, and all evidence is dated 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-23. Its own fuzzer found nine delivery failures in that week; all are reported fixed.
- **It is low-risk to try.** It has no runtime dependencies, the hooks never block a call, it reads only local files by default, and `noonsight uninstall` removes it.

## Conditions and risks

- **Write model-specific rules first.** If you cannot name rules that should differ by model, a `CLAUDE.md` is simpler.
- **Pin Claude Code or re-check on upgrade.** The delivery result holds for 2.1.330 only, and several behaviours it depends on are undocumented by Claude Code. Rerun `npm run delivery -- corpus` (no login or tokens needed) after each Claude Code update.
- **Known gaps for subagents.**

  - Parallel calls of one subagent type that need different rules get nothing until their first Edit, Write or agent call.
  - Subagents from organisation-synced plugins are predicted on the parent's model.
  - Agent teams, routing and the classifier are unmeasured.
- **Fallback models are undeclared.** In the pilot Claude Code switched by itself to Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5, which the preset has no rules for. Those sessions get only a note that the earlier rules no longer apply.
- **Cost goes up.** The pilot cost 7% more per run than no rules, against 19% more for a shared `CLAUDE.md`. `verify-changes` roughly doubled the cost of a small fix.
- **Hook overhead.** Each hook run takes 80 to 150 ms of processor time, and a subagent start can wait up to two seconds more.
- **Team rollout is per person.** Each person installs it and runs `noonsight trust` in each repository with shared rules. The machine-wide install was not checked live.

- **The benchmark is self-graded.** The API was a local stand-in, so no model answered, and the reference for "right rules" is noonsight's own resolver. A wrong resolution would not show.
- **My spot-check was partial.** The `CLAUDE.md` figures in the raw `summary.json` match the README. I did not confirm noonsight's own figures in that file.

- **Known gaps, in its own docs.**

  - Foreground subagent calls of one type that need different rules get nothing until their first edit.

  - **If hooks change:** if a Claude Code update changes hook behavior, deliveries can go missing silently. The decision log records what the hook returned, not what reached the model.
- **The benchmark has blind spots.** It uses a stub API that gives fixed answers. It checks that rules arrive, not that models follow them. Its reference is noonsight's own resolver, so a wrong resolution would not show up. Delivered rules are context only. Use a permission rule or a hook for anything that must never be broken.
- **Provenance and platform.** It is a small project, renamed from "sextant", with a single maintainer's GitHub org visible in the README. Review the hook code and pin the npm version. Install globally rather than via `npx`, because the `npx` hooks stop delivering once npm's cache is cleared. Windows is not supported.
- **Cost.** Extra rules add tokens and can add work. Expect higher spend on Sonnet and Haiku coding tasks. Fable's three-task cost comparison was untested.

**What it guarantees:** Through Claude Code's hooks, it puts the rules declared for a model into every request of each session and subagent running on that model, and re-delivers them when the model changes or the conversation is compacted, cleared, resumed or forked. That rests on 0 failures in 299 randomized real-session runs on Claude Code 2.1.330 (3,090 of 3,090 requests covered), plus a corpus of reproduced failures. It is delivery only, not obedience, and it holds for the Claude Code versions tested.

It does not guarantee the model follows the rules, that a switch's note reaches the model, or that the predicted subagent model is the one it ran on.

I did not run the test suite. This verdict rests on reading the README, the docs, and the 2026-11-19 benchmark results.

**Verdict: adopt with conditions.** Run it as a time-boxed pilot on a few people's machines, pinned to one commit, with routing and the classifier left off. Do not roll it out team-wide yet.

I read the README, the hook contract, the verification notes, the preset sources and the dated experiment results. I did not read the source closely, build it or run its tests, so everything below rests on the project's own documentation and recorded results.

**Reasons**

- **It targets your exact setup.** It gives each session and each subagent only the rules written for the model it runs on, and re-delivers after `/model`, `/clear`, compaction and resume.
- **Delivery beats a shared `CLAUDE.md` in its own tests.** In the delivery fuzz on Claude Code 2.1.328, noonsight covered 99.5% of requests (3 of 300 sessions broke the invariant). On the first 60 sequences:

  | Method | Requests covered | Subagent requests covered |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | noonsight | 100% | 100% |
  | one `CLAUDE.md` with every model's rules | 87.4% | 32.2% |
  | `.claude/rules` | 70.9% | 32.2% |

  The `CLAUDE.md` never reached Explore and Plan subagents, and it gave each model the other models' rules too (only 18–29% of the text a model read was written for it).
- **No measured gain in task success.** In the 588-run benchmark pilot, 133, 132 and 133 of 144 verified tasks resolved under off, noonsight and `CLAUDE.md`. Cost per run was about 7% higher with noonsight, against 19% for the `CLAUDE.md`.
- **Only some rules have a measured effect.**
  - The verify rules made Sonnet and Haiku run tests after a small fix (30 of 30 and 27 of 30, against 0 of 30), at 46–59% more cost on those small tasks.
  - Sonnet's carry-through rule raised complete runs from 9 to 32 of 40 on one task, at low effort and unattended.
  - Fable's report rule shortened sentences.
  - Haiku's carry-through showed no effect, and the Opus rule and Fable's subagent rule are unmeasured.
- **The default preset is mostly dormant in interactive use.**
  - Interactive Opus and Fable sessions receive nothing.
  - Interactive Sonnet and Haiku sessions receive only the verify rule, after their first edit of a git-tracked code file.
  - Subagents get only the every-scope rules (carry-through for Sonnet and Haiku, the report rule for Fable).
  - The rest needs a scope, which nothing sets by default.
- **It is pre-release.** The version is 0.0.1, marked private, "early development", nothing published, and installed from a clone with `npm link`. The last fuzz run found two delivery failures; the changelog says both are fixed, but no fuzz run after those fixes is recorded.
- **It is low-risk to try.** Hooks always exit 0, never deny a call, read only local files, have no runtime dependencies, and write a decision log. `NOONSIGHT_DISABLE=1` or `noonsight uninstall` turns it off.

**Conditions and risks**

Conditions:
- **Pin versions.** Pin a noonsight commit and stay on Claude Code versions it was checked against (2.1.325–2.1.329). Rerun `npm run test:live` and `npm run delivery -- all` before each Claude Code upgrade.
- **Keep routing off.** In auto mode a routed subagent call causes the other agent calls in the same response to be refused and retried, and by default a routed call runs without a permission prompt.
- **Keep the classifier off.** It sends the first 4,000 characters of each task to a model through a person's login and costs usage.
- **Decide how scopes get set.** Otherwise treat the pilot as testing only the verify rules and the subagent rules. Your own team rules can be added per model.
- **Review the decision log weekly.** `noonsight report` shows mismatches, undeclared models and rules never delivered.

Risks:
- **Claude Code internals.** It depends on hook behaviour that was largely observed, not documented, and several facts were checked by hand once. A Claude Code update can silently change what is delivered.
- **Coverage gaps.** Plugin subagents, `--agents` definitions, agent-team teammates and workflow agents are mispredicted or get nothing. A subagent call held on a permission prompt for a couple of minutes loses its rules.
- **Wrong-model cases.**
  - A resume on the default model after compaction is a documented limit.
  - A model set only by MDM is not read.
  - On Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry, aliases need pinning variables.
  - On macOS, a prompt containing `--model x` can confuse the model detection.
- **Fallback models.** When Claude Code switched models by itself (to Opus 4.8 or Sonnet 5 in the pilot), the new model got only a note retiring the old rules, because the preset has no rules for it.
- **Footprint.** It edits `settings.json` in every Claude Code config directory in the home folder, adds roughly 60–120 ms per hook event, and runs a hook on every Edit and Write.
- **Maintenance.** It appears to be a single-author project, and the preset must be updated for each new model version; until then that model gets a warning and no rules.
- **Windows.** I saw live checks recorded only for macOS and Linux.

**What it guarantees**

It guarantees only that its hooks never block or deny anything and that every decision is logged; delivery of the right rules to the right model is best-effort, and rests on Claude Code's hook behaviour as observed on versions 2.1.325–2.1.329, not on any stable contract.
